facts.text: New Salem, Illinois, is the recreated village where Abraham Lincoln lived from 1831 to 1837, complete with period cabins and antiques.
The TimeWalk exhibit in the Visitor Center lets visitors experience New Salem’s history from its original saw and grist mill to the Civilian Conservation Corps reconstruction.
Costumed interpreters in New Salem bring the 1830s to life, explaining daily life for a young Lincoln and his fellow settlers.
Every summer, New Salem hosts Theatre in the Park, a 475‑seat outdoor amphitheater that stages family‑friendly performances in a historic setting.
Lincoln’s New Salem State Historic Site offers walking tours that trace the lane where the former village once stood, showcasing log houses and pioneer life.
The village’s name, New Salem, reflects its origins as a planned community in Menard County, later renamed to honor Lincoln’s early home.
